capitals.name: Ugarit (Ras Shamra)
capitals.note: The page names no formal capital but treats the city of Ugarit (the tell of about 28 hectares) as the kingdom's centre; ports at Minet el-Beida and Ras Ibn Hani.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Ugarit; its Hittite shape of -1300 (321,568 km2) swallows the coast. The page gives the kingdom 'about 2,000 km2 on average' and 'roughly equivalent to the modern Latakia Governorate' at its zenith; the gazetteer's Lattakia governorate is 1,770 km2 (7 cells), inside the page's figure. The Siyannu concession under Niqmaddu II is undated and unplaced on the page, so the shape is not reduced for it.

region.text: the kingdom at its zenith, 'roughly equivalent to the modern Latakia Governorate', about 2,000 km2 on average

ledger.note: c. 1450 BC: the kingdom of Ugarit stands on the Syrian coast. The page says only that the polity 'was at its height c. 1450 to c. 1185 BC'; it gives no founding year (the city is attested in the Mari archive c. 1765 BC and had been a vassal of Yamhad, undated), so the start is a bridging judgment.

region.text: the kingdom at its zenith, 'roughly equivalent to the modern Latakia Governorate', about 2,000 km2 on average

ledger.note: c. 1345 BC (bridged): Ugarit becomes a Hittite vassal. 'Niqmaddu II reigned c. 1350 - c. 1315 BC. Ugarit became a Hittite vassal, first under a viceroy at Karkemis'; the Niqmaddu II page calls him 'a vassal ruler of Suppiluliuma I of Hatti' and dates Suppiluliuma's Mitanni campaigns c. 1350-1345 BC, without dating the submission. Mirrors the hittites dossier.

region.text: the kingdom at its zenith, 'roughly equivalent to the modern Latakia Governorate', about 2,000 km2 on average

ledger.note: c. 1185 BC: the Hittite vassalage ends with the destruction of Ugarit. The infobox date of the destruction is c. 1185 BC; the destruction table c. 1190 BC; radiocarbon and eclipse evidence 1192-1190 BC; Ammurapi (c. 1215 to 1180 BC) is the last king and a contemporary of Suppiluliuma II.

region.text: the kingdom at its zenith, 'roughly equivalent to the modern Latakia Governorate', about 2,000 km2 on average

ledger.note: c. 1185 BC: Ugarit is destroyed. 'The city may have been destroyed around 1192-1190 BC' (Ammurapi page); the Ugarit page's infobox gives c. 1185 BC and says it 'would become one of the many states of the ancient Near East that were destroyed or abandoned'; Ammurapi's letters speak of 'the seven ships of the enemy that came here'. The page names no successor.

wars.name: Revolt of Mukish, Nuhashshe and Niya against Ugarit and Hatti
wars.outcome: Itur-Addu of Mukish, Addu-nirari of Nuhashshe and Agi-Teshub of Niya 'turned hostile'; Suppiluliuma I's treaty with Niqmaddu II (CTH 46) records it. No border change is dated.
wars.note: Year silent on the page; 1345 is the page's date for Suppiluliuma's Mitanni campaigns (c. 1350-1345 BC). Mukish and Nuhashshe have no dossier (see syrian-city-states in the hittites dossier).

wars.name: Destruction of Ugarit by the Sea Peoples

zones.text: the kingdom at its zenith, 'roughly equivalent to the modern Latakia Governorate', about 2,000 km2 on average

wars.outcome: Ugarit destroyed around 1192-1190 BC (infobox c. 1185 BC) after Ammurapi wrote that 'the enemy's ships came' and 'all my ships are in the Land of Lukka'.
wars.note: The Ugarit page's body does not name the Sea Peoples; it speaks of 'the enemy' and 'attacks from outsiders'. The Ammurapi page does not date the letters.

certainty.note: The kingdom is a coastal strip of about 2,000 km2; no treaty line is drawn on any page opened.

sources.title: Ugarit
sources.note: Dates c. 1450-c. 1185 BC, area about 2,000 km2 (Latakia Governorate), kings and reigns, Hittite vassalage, destruction dates.

sources.title: Niqmaddu II
sources.note: Reign c. 1350-1315 BC; Hittite vassal of Suppiluliuma I; Mukish, Nuhashshe and Niya turned hostile; Siyannu conceded to the Amorites (undated).

sources.title: Ammurapi
sources.note: Last king c. 1215-1180 BC; letters about the enemy's ships; destruction c. 1192-1190 BC.

notes: Cliopatria has no Ugarit. The 1450 start is a bridge (the page gives the kingdom's height, not its founding); the 1345 Hittite vassalage mirrors the hittites dossier (me-04-a) and rests on a reign span, not a dated submission. The Niqmaddu II page says Siyannu was 'conceded to the Amorites in a dispute over the Shiyannu region early in his reign' but gives no year and no place; it is not drawn (the Hittite dossier's amurru vassal pair is the neighbour to check). Ugarit's relation to Egypt (Amarna letters EA45, 48, 49; 'good relations') is not vassalage on the page. Yamhad's earlier overlordship (c. 1820 BC onwards, undated) is outside the 1450 start. Ugarit has no successor on the page; the Hittites dossier and the Phoenicia dossier should not be assumed to take its coast. The ruler list was not drawn: the Ugarit page's king table gives c. dates for Ammittamru I (mid-14th century), Niqmaddu II (c. 1350-1315), Arhalba (c. 1315-1313), Niqmepa (c. 1313-1260), Ammittamru II (c. 1260-1235) and Ammurapi (c. 1215-1180) with gaps.
